gap: No result ChatGPT got sets out, in one place, what it costs in software and licences to record four cameras on each option: Synology needs two paid perpetual licences on top of its two free ones. QNAP's QVR Surveillance covers four cameras for free only once you claim 6 'launch campaign' bonus channels through a QNAP ID, and QNAP doesn't say whether they are permanent; QVR Elite gives 2 free. UGREEN publishes no fee, and Reolink's RLN8-410 needs no licence but has 10/100 PoE ports and takes drives of up to 8 TB each.
standout_why: Compared against the cited QNAP FAQ (qnap.com …what-is-the-difference-between-qvr-proelite-and-qvr-surveillance), the Synology Device License Pack pages, the Surveillance Station spec pages, the Reolink RLN8-410 product page and Reolink's Synology guide. Each cited page holds one piece. The QNAP FAQ says '8 free channels' but doesn't say 6 of them are a campaign bonus; that is in the QNAP tutorial, which ChatGPT got at rank 35 but did not cite. The RLN8-410 page states the 8 TB-per-drive limit, but ChatGPT's answers still advised 12–16 TB on that NVR. No page sets the four platforms' licence terms for exactly four cameras side by side. I could not source the dollar total for each option, which would have made the comparison new.
decides: This mostly confirms the picks ChatGPT and our page already give: RLN8-410 for recording only, UGREEN DXP2800 as the NAS with no published camera fee, and Synology for the most mature software, with two paid licences. It corrects our current page: the QNAP TS-264 row says 'QVR Elite: 2 free channels, then subscription only', which is out of date. QNAP's newer QVR Surveillance includes 8 free channels (2 standard + 6 bonus), so the TS-264 can record four cameras with no fee. The catch is that the 6 bonus channels are a launch-campaign claim with no announced end date and no stated permanence, so present the TS-264 as 'free for four if you claim the bonus now'. For the RLN8-410, the 8 TB-per-drive limit means one internal drive holds about 31 days for four cameras at 6 Mbps each (ChatGPT's own 7.8 TB figure). Longer retention needs a second drive on eSATA, up to 16 TB in total.

findings.label: Storage limit
findings.value: 8 TB per HDD; 16 TB total (8 TB internal SATA + 8 TB eSATA); ships with 2 TB
findings.source_title: Reolink RLN8-410 | NVR for Up to 12 Cameras & 24/7 Recording
findings.note: Four cameras at 6 Mbps = 2.59 TB/day decimal (4×6e6/8×86,400), so one 8 TB internal drive holds about 31 days. This is where it loses to a NAS for longer retention without an eSATA drive.

findings.label: Free camera channels, QVR Surveillance vs Elite vs Pro
findings.value: QVR Surveillance: 8 free (2 standard + 6 bonus), up to 1,024 channels, lifetime or subscription licences; QVR Pro: 8 built-in, perpetual; QVR Elite: 2 free, subscription-focused
findings.source_title: What is the difference between QVR Pro/Elite and QVR Surveillance? | QNAP
findings.note: This makes our page's TS-264 row ('QVR Elite… subscription only') out of date

findings.label: How the 6 bonus channels are claimed
findings.value: Sign in with a QNAP ID (myQNAPcloud), then QVR Surveillance > Help > Feature Tour > 'Claim now'. Called a 'launch campaign'; 'QNAP has not announced an end date'
findings.source_title: How to Claim 6 Additional Free Channels in QVR Surveillance? | QNAP
findings.note: The article does not say whether claimed channels are permanent or list eligible models. Without the claim you get 2 free channels, which is short of four cameras. That is where it can lose.
